claims.claim: Legacy oauth.json is parsed with JSON.parse on the raw file text, so a UTF-8 BOM makes parsing throw and the OAuth credentials are silently skipped while an auth.json with only apiKeys is written, permanently blocking the OAuth migration.

The repair only strips the BOM before parsing (reusing the existing stripBom helper already used for settings.json and keybindings.json) and rejects non-object oauth.json payloads before anything is renamed, so malformed legacy files stay on disk unchanged.

OAuth precedence and apiKeys fallback are preserved: migrated providers carry type "oauth" and settings.json apiKeys are only applied when the provider was not already migrated, then removed from settings.json.
An existing auth.json still short-circuits the migration before any read/write/rename, so it is never modified.

The regression executes the real migrateAuthToAuthJson through .prale-eval/subject.mjs and asserts BOM migration, OAuth precedence, apiKeys fallback, malformed-input preservation and untouched existing auth.json; it fails with an assertion on the original fault and passes on the repaired code.

validation.notes: Ran from the workspace root with Node 24.14.0; all 4 regression checks passed and the process exited 0. The script loads the real packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts via .prale-eval/subject.mjs loadMigrations(root, agentDir) with real fs/path and a caller-owned agent dir under .prale-eval/.tmp-regression (removed afterwards). Checked: (1) oauth.json written as '\uFEFF{...}' now migrates both providers into auth.json with type "oauth" and byte-preserved access/refresh/expires, and the legacy file is renamed to oauth.json.migrated retaining its credentials; (2) when settings.json apiKeys collide with an OAuth provider, the OAuth credential wins, the apiKey is not written, the non-colliding apiKey migrates as type "api_key", apiKeys is dropped from settings.json and unrelated settings survive; (3) a truncated BOM-prefixed oauth.json stays byte-identical with no .migrated copy and no invented provider entry while apiKeys still migrate as fallback; (4) an existing auth.json (contents unchanged, including its BOM and trailing newline) makes the migration return [] and leaves oauth.json and settings.json untouched. Fault detection was verified by temporarily restoring the baseline migrations.ts (git checkout of that single file) and re-running the same command: it exited 1 with AssertionError 'BOM-prefixed oauth.json providers must be reported as migrated' (actual [], expected ['anthropic','custom-provider']), then exited 0 again after re-applying the repair. No dependencies or network were required; optional repository typecheck/vitest suites were not run because node_modules is absent in this environment, so only the Node TypeScript-strip load and the VM-based regression were used.
